sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, SQL Server and Azure SQL: Automatic tuning
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: plan choice regression, where 'the new plan might cause a performance regression, such as a parameter sensitivity or parameter sniffing related issue'; 'you should find a previous good plan and force it ... by using the sp_query_store_force_plan procedure' (EXEC sp_query_store_force_plan 12, 17: query_id, plan_id); 'force the last known good plan because older plans might be invalid'; manually forced plans 'should not be forced forever'; ALTER DATABASE ... SET AUTOMATIC_TUNING (FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN = ON), which depends on Query Store; sys.dm_db_tuning_recommendations shows detected regressions. The ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION reference (read 2026-11-18): CLEAR PROCEDURE_CACHE 'Clears the procedure (plan) cache for the database'; a plan handle limits it to one plan.

brief.situation: You are the database administrator at Haldane Freight. Since 10:05 the customer portal's order search has gone from 40 ms to 6 seconds and the database's CPU is at 95%. Last night's maintenance updated statistics on dbo.Shipments. At 11:00 the carriers' bulk status check starts, which runs the same search 30,000 times.
handover: Query Store is on (READ_WRITE) for the database; automatic tuning is off.
The database is Azure SQL Database, Business Critical, 8 vCores; no schema changes were deployed.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the order search query, its plans in Query Store and the database's CPU.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the search slowed, what you forced and why that plan, and what keeps it from recurring.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: Query 4127 took 95% of CPU. It had run plan 31 (index seek, about 40 ms) for six weeks; at 02:14, after the statistics update, it compiled plan 88, a scan sized for the largest customer, about 6 seconds for everyone.

parts.label: Forced
parts.criteria: Last known good, one query only.
parts.modelAnswer: sp_query_store_force_plan for query 4127 and plan 31, the last known good plan; the engine's own recommendation agreed. Clearing the plan cache would have recompiled everything at peak.

parts.label: Recurrence
parts.criteria: Automates the guard and fixes the cause.
parts.modelAnswer: FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN is on, and a ticket addresses the query's parameter sensitivity so the forced plan can be removed after review.

recompileStorm.headline: A cache flush is a shotgun
recompileStorm.body: Query Store already showed which query regressed and which plan was good. Force that plan for that query; do not make the whole database recompile at peak.

portalDown.headline: The good plan was in Query Store
portalDown.body: When a plan regresses, Query Store keeps the history: find the last good plan and force it with sp_query_store_force_plan.

forced.headline: Good: Query Store used as intended
forced.body: You found the query and its two plans, saw the regression after the statistics update, forced the last good plan, checked it, and set up automatic correction while the parameter sensitivity is fixed.

scoring.modelReasoning: Query Store shows one query using the CPU and two plans for it: the seek plan that ran for weeks and a scan plan compiled after last night's statistics update, sized for the largest customer. Force the last known good plan for that query only, then check. Clearing the plan cache recompiles everything at peak and may produce the same plan; rebuilding the index changes nothing. Turn on FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN and fix the parameter sensitivity so the forced plan can be removed.
